reading.body:
James Risch's AI record is mostly money and one bill: three Anthropic PAC contributions and two Google NetPAC contributions of $2,500 each, plus a cosponsorship of S. 1633.

The contributions cluster in two periods. Google NetPAC gave $2,500 in November 2025 and again in July 2026. Anthropic's PAC gave $2,500 in August 2026, then two more of $2,500 on the same day, August 27, 2026. One of those same-day entries is recorded as negative $2,500, which the data does not explain. Amazon's PAC gave $2,500 in July 2025. All five positive contributions are the same size, which is the pattern of a committee writing uniform checks rather than of escalating support.

The legislative side is thinner than the money side. The only AI bill in the record is S. 1633, the TEST AI Act of 2025, cosponsored on May 7, 2025. The other twelve entries are all votes on S. 2296, a bill with no short title on file, taken across September and October 2025. Risch voted Yea on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on the motion to table an amendment, and on passage, and split Yea and Nay across eight amendment votes on the same day. Nothing in the data says what S. 2296 does or whether it concerns AI at all.

What this does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no vote or contribution tied to data centers, transmission, power procurement, or any of the physical constraints on AI scaling. The record shows a senator taking uniform PAC money from three large technology companies and voting on one unnamed bill, and it does not connect the two.
